newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Distrigas, Ruhrgas sign transit contract.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Distrigas, Ruhrgas sign transit contract.

text.p: Belgian natural gas distributor Distrigas/Distrigaz said on Monday it had signed a transit contract with Germany's Ruhrgas to transport British gas to the German border via the Belgian port of Zeebrugge.

"Based on (the contract), British natural gas, bought by Ruhrgas in Britain, can be transported between Zeebrugge and Eynatten at the Belgo-Dutch border from the end of 1998," Distrigas said in a statement.
Distrigas, a unit of Belgian utility holding company Tractebel, had already announced a similar transit deal with German Wingas for gas bought in Britain.
British Petroleum Co Plc said earlier on Monday it signed a $1 billion, 15-year contract to supply gas to Ruhrgas from October next year.

Distrigas said last month it would invest 12 to 15 billion Belgian francs ($358 to $448 million) to boost the gas transit capacity of its network from its Interconnector terminal in Zeebrugge to four points at Belgium's borders.
The 240-km (149 miles) Interconnector pipeline, the first gas pipeline to link Britain with continental Europe, is due to come on stream in October 1998.
Distrigas spokesman Yves Panneels told Reuters that the transit contracts which had already been signed represented more than half the Interconnector's annual capacity of 20 billion cubic metres.

Other companies which have signed transit contracts with Distrigas have declined to announce the deal as they were still negotiating with gas producers and did not want to undermine their bargaining position.
